headings.title: SMTO-GML-0053 — Gmail isn't showing a folder or feature SMTO needs

html:
SMTO-GML-0053 — Gmail isn't showing a folder or feature SMTO needs

GUID: 6588f89c-a87f-59af-b44c-23f69e77bed2
Slug: gmail-imap-feature-required
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail_imap

What happened

  • To do this safely, SMTO needs Gmail to show certain folders, such as All Mail, Drafts and Trash, and some mailbox features to email apps. One of them isn't available, so SMTO stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Gmail on the web, open Settings › See all settings › Labels. Make sure Show in IMAP is ticked for All Mail, Drafts and Trash. SMTO uses these folders to find, draft and remove mail, and stops if Gmail hides them from email apps.
  2. If the Gmail address belongs to a work or school, ask its Google administrator whether full mailbox access for email apps is allowed. An administrator setting can hide mailbox features that SMTO relies on.
  3. Before asking again, check Gmail to see whether any part of the request, such as a new draft or moved message, already happened. Earlier steps of the same request may have finished before SMTO reached the missing feature.
  4. Ask SMTO to test the Gmail connection with the same account, then ask only for what is still missing. The test checks that Gmail now shows the needed folders without changing any mail.

What success looks like

  • The Gmail connection test succeeds, and the request finishes with no duplicate drafts or moves in Gmail.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If Gmail can't provide the feature, ask them about a Gmail account that signs in through Google; don't switch accounts in the middle of this request.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gmail IMAP session lacked a required capability or folder: the X-GM-EXT-1 extension, a selectable All Mail special-use folder, MOVE (trash and delete), UIDPLUS (draft creation), or the Drafts or Trash special-use folder.

What this means

  • The server did not expose a required Gmail extension, UID operation or special-use folder. Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.

Why this can happen

  • Producer condition: The server did not expose a required Gmail extension, UID operation or special-use folder.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact account revision, Gateway route and failing substep with the retained receipt.

How to fix it

  • Check the account's IMAP folder visibility (Gmail Settings › Labels › Show in IMAP for All Mail, Drafts and Trash) and any Workspace policy limiting IMAP. Trash and permanent deletion need MOVE, draft creation needs UIDPLUS, and session start needs X-GM-EXT-1 plus a \All folder; for configurations that cannot provide these, use an explicitly selected OAuth account.
  • Check Gmail IMAP access and folder visibility with the account administrator. Trash needs UID MOVE, draft creation needs UIDPLUS, and mailbox discovery needs Gmail extensions and All Mail. Use an OAuth account for unsupported server configurations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Preserve confirmed work and establish the current mailbox state before any repeated write.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen operation completes with a matching receipt, or the remaining uncertain action is inspected in Gmail without duplicate mail.

What not to do

  • Do not switch accounts or authentication methods after failure, or automatically replay uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.
  • App-password setup: https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
